title: Multi-leader replication and write conflicts

kcs.statement: Multi-leader replication lets more than one node accept writes, typically one leader per region, so writes stay local and a region's loss does not stop writes elsewhere.
Two leaders can accept conflicting writes to the same record before they sync, so a multi-leader setup needs a conflict-resolution rule.
Last-write-wins keeps the write with the latest timestamp and silently discards the other, which loses data when writes are concurrent or clocks are skewed.

problem_ideas: Two users in US and EU rename the same shared doc within 100 ms: show what last-write-wins keeps
